title: Tight ratio for known-i.i.d. online stochastic matching
short_statement: In the known-i.i.d. online stochastic matching model, offline vertices and the type distribution are known, online types arrive independently, and matches are irrevocable. What is the exact optimal competitive ratio against the offline optimum?
open_problem: Determine the optimal competitive ratio for known-i.i.d. online stochastic bipartite matching, including whether the gap between the best algorithms and the known upper bound can be closed for the original unweighted model and its weighted variants.
full_statement: In the known-i.i.d. online stochastic matching model, there is a fixed set of offline vertices and a known distribution over online vertex types. At each period, an online type is sampled independently from this distribution; after seeing its incident offline neighbors, the algorithm must either match it immediately to an unmatched compatible offline vertex or discard it. The benchmark is the expected size or weight of the offline optimum that knows the entire arrival sequence. Manshadi, Oveis Gharan, and Saberi gave a $0.702$-competitive algorithm for the original model, $0.705$ under integral rates, and an upper bound of $0.823$ for every online algorithm. Later work improved several weighted and integral-rate variants, but the exact optimal ratio in the basic known-i.i.d. model remains unknown. The open problem is to close this constant-factor gap and identify the structural algorithm or hard instance that determines the true ratio.
known_results: The adversarial online bipartite matching ratio is exactly $1-1/e$, while the known-i.i.d. model can beat this barrier. Feldman-Mehta-Mirrokni-Muthukrishnan initiated the model and obtained improvements under integral expected arrivals. Manshadi, Oveis Gharan, and Saberi removed the integrality need for beating $1-1/e$ and proved a universal upper bound of $0.823$. Brubach, Sankararaman, Srinivasan, and Xu later improved ratios for important variants, including weighted-edge and vertex-weighted integral-rate settings. The broad constant gap between lower and upper bounds in the original known-i.i.d. model is still the clean unresolved part.

where_posed.text: Gap left by Manshadi, Oveis Gharan, and Saberi, 'Online Stochastic Matching: Online Actions Based on Offline Statistics', and subsequent known-i.i.d. online stochastic matching work.
